### Keeping History Alive: Blanchard Junior Knockabout Restoration

![4Culture logo](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c48db894eddeca43abfade1/1571096588084-FYHMC8XW8IBYAFXC8CXO/4+culture)

Two Blanchard Junior Knockabouts (BJKs) have been relaunched after extensive restoration, funded in part by 4Culture. The work was the first project in the new Bill Garden Boatshop in the Wagner Education Center.

The Center caretakes seven BJKs, designed and built by Norm Blanchard on Lake Union between the 1930s and 1960s. They are used daily for rentals and sailing classes.

**V. Velez** was hauled out in November 2018 with support from CSR Marine in Ballard. After a collision, she needed new frames, deck, and planking. The work used white oak frames, larch garboard planks, okoume plywood for the deck, and a Sitka spruce mast, with lumber sourced together with shipwright Ben Kahn. Milling the lumber required professional-grade shop tools, most of them donated or funded by donors.

Three boatwrights and many volunteer hours went into the project. Orion Marion started it in fall 2018, Josh Anderson continued it through the winter, and Dustin Espey oversaw the heavy lifting and hull work.

**PAMALA** received new garboard planks, had her seams below the waterline resealed with cotton and putty, and was re-bedded on her keel to improve watertightness.

Today both boats are "nearly good as new, despite being over seventy years old." The Center plans ongoing restoration, new boatbuilding, and continued maintenance of the BJK fleet — and volunteers are invited to join the boatshop.
